item.title: Medieval guilds kept secrets alive by making apprentices rebuild the same tools
item.description: Historians studying guild records found that apprentices were required to remake the master's tools from scratch every few years. Rather than writing down methods, the guilds preserved know-how by repeating the act of making.

item.title: The board game that taught Victorian children to navigate railways
item.description: A 19th-century board game simplified the British railway network into a few rules about connections and transfers. Players learned the network's structure by playing, not by memorizing timetables, a design that discarded accuracy for teachability.
